title: Quarterly self-audit sprintbook — Sophie Martinez
content:
Purpose:
A concise, action-oriented notebook to prepare for my Q4 calibration + 1:1 with my manager. Focus: evidence-first narrative, clear asks, and a 90-day sprint plan with measurable signals. This is a working doc — mix of bullets, short scripts, and evidence snippets for quick copy-paste into the meeting chat or my self-review form.

TL;DR (two lines):
- Delivered new onboarding checklist + two hiring playbooks that cut time-to-ramp for new ops hires by ~25% (pilot).
- Need a focused reallocation (0.2 FTE) and approval to run a compensation calibration experiment for senior IC benchmark alignment.

Key outcomes last quarter (what I shipped / impact):
- Onboarding checklist (pilot): reduced average first-30-day ticket volume for new hires from 18 -> 13 (pilot group, n=8).
- Hiring playbooks x2: Technical Recruiter -> People Ops Partner handoff SOP; Interview loop rubric for IC6+ roles. Used in 5 reqs, received positive feedback from Eng hiring managers.
- Ad-hoc incident support (2 P1 on-call rotations): shortened incident postmortem turnaround by 40% via templated response and task assignment matrix.
- People analytics dashboard prototype: baseline churn signals + manager view created; used in one thoughtful calibration session.

Measurable signals (metrics I own / care about):
- Time-to-ramp (first 30 days): target 20% reduction by end of Q2 next cycle. Current pilot improvement: 25% in pilot subset.
- Offer acceptance delta for senior ICs: +5% target after playbooks and streamlined loop. Current: +2% (small n).
- PMF of onboarding materials (manager survey): target 4.2/5; current average 3.8 across 12 managers.
- Incidents: mean PM response time post-rotation reduced from 8h -> 4.8h.

Evidence snippets (copyable to review):
- "Onboarding checklist pilot metrics (internal): new hires (n=8) average ticket count first-30-days = 13 vs org average 18. Source: HR-2345."
- "Hiring playbook used in hiring for Search infra IC6 req (REQ-4891). Hiring manager feedback: 'Faster alignment on must-have vs nice-to-have, saved ~2 interviews.'"
- Links: Confluence: People Ops Q4 initiative brief; Slack thread: #hiring-feedback; PR: github.com/redwood/ops-docs/pull/312 (playbook updates).

Anecdotes / qualitative notes:
- Manager A pulled me into a hiring triage call and said the playbook 'stopped the loop from cycling'. Feels like early momentum for standardization.
- One new hire commented that the checklist removed '90% of the onboarding guesswork' — anecdotal but matches the ticket-drop trend.

What didn't go well / root causes:
- Dashboard adoption low: managers didn't adopt because 1) not surfaced in OKR syncs and 2) too many clicks.
- Offer acceptance improvement smaller than expected: candidate feed shows compensation anchors were misaligned at benchmark level. Need comp experiment.

My core asks for the manager (specific, measurable):
- Approve a 0.2 FTE reallocation from project work to run a 6-week comp benchmarking experiment (scope: senior IC offers, 10 hires window). Success signal: +7% offer acceptance delta or playbook adoption >80%.
- Sponsor a 2-hour ops playbook review with hiring managers (calendar coordination + headcount owners).
- Support for a 'dashboard adoption' nudge: ask product analytics to add a one-click manager summary to the weekly sync (approx 2 days eng effort).

Manager prep script (25–45s soundbites I can use):
- "Quick snapshot — onboarding pilot reduced first-30-day tickets 25% in the pilot group (n=8). I need a small reallocation to scale the playbook and run a compensation experiment to close the senior offer gap."
- "If we can get 0.2 FTE and run the experiment with 10 hires, we should see measurable changes within one quarter."

90-day sprint plan (high level):
- Week 1–2: finalize comp experiment design (benchmarks, acceptance metrics, control group). Align with finance/comp.
- Week 3–6: run experiment (apply to live offers for eligible senior IC reqs), collect feedback, and adjust playbook pricing guidance.
- Week 7–9: scale onboarding playbook to 2 additional teams, run manager adoption workshops.
- Week 10–12: consolidate learnings, write postmortem + recommendation to leadership, and propose permanent headcount change if signals positive.

Mini-checklist for experiment design (quick):
- Define control vs test reqs (10 total).
- Establish acceptance metrics + timeframe (30-day acceptance; ramp follow-up at 90 days).
- Finance sign-off for temporary comp delta budget.
- Legal/People ops sign-off on offer language templates.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: small n and hiring season noise -> mitigate by lengthening window or using historical comparator.
- Risk: manager bandwidth to adopt playbook -> mitigate via 1-pager + 30-min office hours + PM ownership for rollout.

Questions I want to hear from manager (priority order):
- Is a temporary 0.2 FTE reallocation realistic given org priorities?
- Are you comfortable sponsoring the comp experiment to finance?
- Would you like me to present the early pilot data to the hiring guild next week?

Meeting agenda (10–15 min):
1) Quick wins (2 min): onboarding pilot numbers + incident POA.
2) Ask (3 min): 0.2 FTE + comp experiment approval.
3) Roadmap (3–4 min): 90-day plan & adoption plan.
4) Manager feedback & decisions (5 min).

Post-meeting wrap (for me):
- If approved: draft experiment ticket in Jira, assign stakeholders, calendar invites for playbook review session.
- If delayed: propose fallback (pilot scaling limited to one additional team) and capture reasons.

TODO (short sticky list):
- [ ] Draft Jira ticket for comp experiment (HR-2345 follow-up).
- [ ] Share 1-pager with hiring managers + calendar invite.
- [ ] Quick UX tweak request for dashboard one-click summary.
- [ ] Write self-review bullet points using the evidence snippets above.

Notes to self (voice mem style):
- Keep narrative outcome-focused. Avoid over-indexing on activity ("I ran workshops") — lead with impact (metrics + manager quotes).
- Bring two backup asks: one smaller (time-limited pilot scale) and one bolder (headcount).

Open questions I need to resolve before review submission:
- Confirm finance owner for temporary comp budget (ping Diana in finance).
- Pull historical offer-acceptance baseline for senior ICs (ask recruiting analytics).

Last-minute copy to paste into self-review form (short):
"Led onboarding checklist pilot and two hiring playbooks that resulted in a 25% reduction in first-30-day support tickets in the pilot group (n=8). Reduced PM response times during on-call rotations by 40% using templated postmortem/assignment flows. Seeking approval for a 6-week comp experiment (0.2 FTE) to validate pay alignment for senior ICs; success = +7% offer acceptance delta or >80% playbook adoption."

-- end of sprintbook --

(keep this doc as my working artifact; I will snapshot into 'self-review-final' when I'm done editing.)
